samples.xml_description: Implement a module for pulse detection. Clock signal. Reset signal (active low). One-bit input signal. Output signal indicating the presence of pulses. 0. Initial state. A state waiting for pulse 0. 1. A state waiting for pulse 1. 2. A state waiting for pulse 0. 3. A state waiting for pulse 1. With a sequencial logic, must construct this logic as reg declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other combinational or sequencial logic states. sequencial logic. With a combinational logic, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this combinational logic can be declared as a reg but only be used in always(*) block. combinational logic. With a combinational logic operation, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword assign to construct description of this combinational logic operation. combinational logic operation. In the reset condition (~rst_n), set the state register to the initial state and set the data_out output to 0, indicating no pulse. Otherwise, the indicating signal data_out is 1 if pulse_level2 reaches s2 and data_in is 0. Otherwise, returns to 0 until the corresponding pulse appears again. With a sequencial logic operation, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description. sequencial logic operation. If rst_n is inactive, pulse_level1 is reset to 0. Otherwise, pulse_level1 is set to pulse_level2. With a combinational logic operation, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword assign to construct description of this combinational logic operation. combinational logic operation. In case pulse_level1 is s0, if data_in is 0, pulse_level2 is set to s1, else pulse_level2 is set to s0. In case pulse_level1 is s1, if data_in is 1, pulse_level2 is set to s2, else pulse_level2 is set to s1. In case pulse_level1 is s2, if data_in is 0, pulse_level2 is set to s3, else pulse_level2 is set to s0. In case pulse_level1 is s3, if data_in is 1, pulse_level2 is set to s2, else pulse_level2 is set to s1. Declare the module pulse_detect with input and output ports as specified in the ports statement. Declare a register state pulse_level1 to keep track of the current state of the pulse detection process pulse_level2. module pulse_detect ( input clk, input rst_n, input data_in, output data_out ); reg pulse_level1; Give initial value to pulse_level1. In this example, the initial value is s0. Note that this initial block is not required in a hardware description language like Verilog, but it is used here for clarity to show when the simulation starts. initial begin pulse_level1 = s0; end Update pulse_level1 based on the value of pulse_level2. If rst_n is inactive, pulse_level1 is reset to 0. Otherwise, pulse_level1 is set to pulse_level2. always @(posedge clk) begin if (~rst_n) begin pulse_level1 <= s0; end else begin pulse_level1 <= pulse_level2; end end Declare a combinational logic pulse_level2. In this example, pulse_level2 is initially set to s0. Note that this initial block is not required in a hardware description language like Verilog, but it is used here for clarity to show when the simulation starts. reg pulse_level2 = s0; endcode> Update pulse_level2 based on the value of pulse_level1 and data_in. In case pulse_level1 is s0, if data_in is 0, pulse_level2 is set to s1, else pulse_level2 is set to s0. In case pulse_level1 is s1, if data_in is 1, pulse_level2 is set to s2, else pulse_level2 is set to s1. In case pulse_level1 is s2, if data_in is 0, pulse_level2 is set to s3, else pulse_level2 is set to s0. In case pulse_level1 is s3, if data_in is 1, pulse_level2 is set to s2, else pulse_level2 is set to s1. always @(*) begin case (pulse_level1) s0: begin if (data_in == 0) begin pulse_level2 = s1; end else begin pulse_level2 = s0; end end s1: begin if (data_in == 1) begin pulse_level2 = s2; end else begin pulse_level2 = s1; end end s2: begin if (data_in == 0) begin pulse_level2 = s3; end else begin pulse_level2 = s0; end end s3: begin if (data_in == 1) begin pulse_level2 = s2; end else begin pulse_level2 = s1; end end endcase end Assign data_out based on the value of pulse_level2 and data_in. In this example, data_out is assigned a value of 1 if pulse_level2 is s2 and data_in is 0, otherwise data_out is assigned a value of 0. assign data_out = (pulse_level2 == s2 && data_in == 0) ? 1 : 0; endcode> End of module pulse_detect. endmodule
